newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end 1.25 pct up on Wall Street rise.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end 1.25 pct up on Wall Street rise.

text.p: * Broad-based buying due to change in sentiment
Wall Street's record close last week gave Manila shares a long-awaited boost in sentiment on Monday, with the local index closing 1.25 percent, or 39.33 points, to 3,233.67, traders said.
"More than anything else, it was a turnaround in sentiment - from tentative to positive," said Lito Vicencio, manager of Peregrine Securities.
On Friday, the Dow Jones index surged 66.58 points to close at a record 5,838.52 on data showing moderate economic growth and tamed inflation, allaying fears of a hike in U.S. interest rate.
Traders said the Manila market saw broad-based buying, with 63 winners trouncing 46 losers.
Newly-listed mall operator Ever-Gotesco Resources Holdings and Holdings Inc benefited from the improved setiment, closing at 1.14 pesos from an offer price of one peso.
Key index stock Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co gained 15 pesos to 1,635 pesos in line with its 0.25-cent rise to $61.25 in New York on Friday.
